claims.text: The SGD 4.00 the rider contests is the ERP pass-through line for the ECP (Fort Rd towards City) gantry, and the rider was made to pay that one crossing twice: once in cash at the gantry and again on the app ledger. The driver does not deny the cash collection - his own filed statement says that if the app also charged the toll, 'refund him the app one' - and the payments ledger shows the app did charge it, a SGD 4.00 erp line. POL-RD-09 opens with the rule that government-set and third-party pass-through charges are settled separately and are 'never counted twice'; a duplicate pass-through line is refunded in full as a standalone billing-integrity correction, and POL-RD-09(4) makes that correction available whether or not a deviation exists. No deviation finding is needed to reach it.

The toll the rider is contesting is not a charge their own itinerary would ever have produced. The platform's optimal route for this trip is PIE then Nicoll Hwy and carries zero ERP - optimal_route_erp_sgd is 0.0 - while the gantry actually billed, ECP (Fort Rd towards City) at SGD 4.00, is flagged on_optimal_route false. The rider therefore paid a toll incurred by the driver's routing, not by the rider's journey, and that off-route ERP falls to be corrected as a pass-through under POL-RD-09 rather than left on the rider's bill.

The ECP routing was the driver's election, not a rider instruction. The in-app chat log for this trip carries zero messages and no waypoint_hint, so there is no recorded rider request for the expressway and POL-RD-04's rider-requested-detour exoneration cannot be run at all - on the clause's own terms the corroboration test is undecidable and the clause is unavailable. POL-RD-09(3) withholds an ERP refund only where the detour was rider-caused under POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05 or POL-RD-12; none of those is engaged, so nothing on this record bars correction of the ECP toll.

The driver cannot explain the ECP routing away as a closure-forced detour. No traffic advisory covers this trip at all: EV-ADVIS-00523-01 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0 and fired the issue MISSING_ARTIFACT - I disclose that impairment - and its absence leaves POL-RD-03 with no advisory to name an affected road, no validity window and no shortest-lawful-alternative length to compute a cap from. With no closure, no advisory and no rider instruction, the ECP route and the toll it attracted are simply the driver's own choice, and the absence of the advisory is itself citable.

The gantry crossing itself is real, which is exactly why the app line is the duplicate and not the legitimate charge. The driver's own trace carries a fix 0.0 m from the billed gantry at 15:43:10, so the vehicle passed directly through it and the rider does not dispute that the toll was incurred. What the rider disputes is paying it twice for one crossing - cash at the gantry plus the SGD 4.00 app line - and that single duplicated line is what POL-RD-09 corrects.

I do not overreach on distance, and the rider's case does not need it. The trace excess is 1.33 km, or 6.72%, which is below POL-RD-01's 20% establishment threshold, so no route deviation under POL-RD-01 is established and none is claimed here. The contested SGD 4.00 is the twice-charged ERP line, and that line is corrected under POL-RD-09 on its own footing, independently of any deviation finding.

The rider is not a serial deviation claimant, so no extra corroboration is owed. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, which means the POL-RD-08 uplift that would demand corroboration beyond the gps_trace for a rider with four or more unsubstantiated claims is not engaged. I cite that field only for the POL-RD-08 test that names it, as POL-GEN-01 requires; it is used to show no additional burden attaches, never as a substitute for evidence about this trip.

The deviation fails at the first gate, so the rider's core complaint cannot be sustained. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed BOTH 20% of optimal_distance_km AND 0.8 km absolute, and both tests must pass. On the governing trace figure the excess is 1.33 km — which clears the absolute limb — but it is only 6.72% of the 19.8 km optimal, well under the 20% percentage limb. The percentage test therefore fails, no deviation is established, and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip, save only for a billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4).

The threshold test must be run on the trace figure, not on the rounded convenience copy: POL-RD-01 states that gps_trace.trace_distance_km governs where it and trip_record.actual_distance_km disagree, and that actual_distance_km may NOT be cited for the test. The trace itself is sound — 181 fixes at a 10 s cadence, 100% coverage, max_gap_sec 0.0 and no interruptive gap — so no POL-RD-07 impairment arises and the 21.13 km measurement stands as the basis for the 6.72% excess figure.

The 4.00 ERP line is a genuine metered pass-through, not a billing defect. The ECP (Fort Rd towards City) gantry charged at 15:43:10 is met by the trace at a nearest-fix distance of 0.0 m (fix index 99, timestamp 15:43:10), squarely inside the 250 m match radius POL-RD-09 applies. POL-RD-09(4) permits a billing-integrity refund only for a charge line for a gantry the gps_trace NEVER passes; this trace passes this gantry, so limb (4) is not engaged.

The 6.00 airport surcharge is properly chargeable and is no defect: the trip ORIGINATED at Changi Airport Terminal 3 (pickup label on the trip record), and the fare model makes such a surcharge a billing defect only on a trip that does not originate at an airport. Combined with the trace-matched ERP line, no line of this fare_breakdown is a phantom or unmatched charge, so POL-RD-09(4) has nothing to reach.

The rider's account of an in-app exchange — that the driver recommended the expressway and that he agreed — has no documentary support. The chat log for this trip contains zero messages (message_count 0, first_message_at and last_message_at null), so no rider instruction, no detour request and no discussion of a cash toll appears anywhere in the bundle. POL-RD-08 places the initial burden on the rider and provides that assertions citing no evidence ID carry no weight and are discarded.

Even taking the rider's double-payment account at its highest, the 4.00 app ERP charge is a separate, trace-matched metered pass-through for a gantry the vehicle actually crossed; any cash the driver separately collected is an off-platform cash-handling matter between the parties, not a defective platform fare line. POL-RD-09(4) is the sole refund route POL-RD-01 leaves open where no deviation is established, and it does not authorise refunding a matched gantry — so the rider's own 'paid twice' theory, even if credited, supplies no basis to disturb this fare.

This dispute is rider-filed and the fare_breakdown shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00. POL-GEN-03 makes NO_ACTION party-relative: it leaves the present payment state exactly as it stands and never means 'restore the charge'. The correct outcome on this record therefore leaves the 38.83 charged total, including its 4.00 ERP line, in place in the driver's favour.

No repeat-deviation pattern can be weighed against the driver. The excess of 6.72% and 1.33 km falls far short of POL-RD-01's materiality gate of 50% or 8.0 km, so the POL-RD-06 driver_profile check is not even required; and in any event the only citable trailing counter, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d, is 0 across 250 completed trips in 90 days. POL-GEN-01 forbids substituting the lifetime prior_deviation_flags for that field, so there is no pattern evidence here at all.

ruling.explanation: To the rider and the driver — the route is not the issue either of you thinks it is, and the toll is. On the route: the governing measurement is the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00523) at 21.13 km against the platform's 19.8 km optimal, an excess of 1.33 km or 6.7%. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to clear BOTH 20% and 0.8 km. The 0.8 km limb passes; the 20% limb fails, so no deviation is established and no distance-and-time refund is available. The driver's case is accepted on that point, and the trace itself is unimpaired (181 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps), so nothing turns on POL-RD-07. The two pass-through lines the driver defends are also real: the trace carries a fix on the ECP (Fort Rd towards City) gantry at 15:43:10, so the vehicle crossed it and the SGD 4.00 ERP line is not a phantom charge, and the SGD 6.00 airport surcharge is properly chargeable because the trip originated at Changi Airport Terminal 3. Neither is a billing-integrity defect under POL-RD-09(4). What the driver cannot defend is the duplication. The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00523) shows the app charged SGD 4.00 for that gantry, and the driver's own filed statement admits he collected cash for the same toll ('I told him about the cash...') and says that if the app also charged it, 'refund him the app one.' A government pass-through cannot be counted twice: once the toll was paid in cash at the gantry, the ledger line for the same crossing is duplicative and is corrected as a standalone pass-through under POL-RD-09, available whether or not a deviation exists, so the failure of the deviation claim does not touch it. Figures used: ERP line charged SGD 4.00; refund SGD 4.00, which is the whole contested amount (charged total on the trip was SGD 38.83). The empty chat log (EV-CHAT-00523, zero messages) means no rider-requested detour could be run and no rider instruction exists; the missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00523-01, weight 0.0) means no closure defence exists; neither is needed and neither changes the toll correction. The driver profile shows no repeat-deviation pattern (deviation_flags_90d 0 across 250 trips in 90 days, and the deviation is not material), so no POL-RD-06 conduct referral arises. Confidence 0.85: the duplicate-payment fact is carried by the fare breakdown (weight 1.0) and by the driver's admission against his own interest; no impaired artifact carries it, and no escalation is triggered. No referral is ordered: POL-RD-09(4) produces one only for a gantry the trace never passes or a surcharge wrongly applied, and neither is present here.

To both parties, here is the ruling.

1) The route complaint does not establish a deviation. POL-RD-01 requires the excess over the optimal route to beat BOTH 20% and 0.8 km. Measured on the governing GPS figure (EV-GPS-00523, trace_distance_km 21.13 km) against the platform optimal (EV-TRIP-00523, optimal_distance_km 19.8 km), the excess is 1.33 km — over the absolute limb but only 6.72% of optimal, under the 20% limb. The percentage test fails, so no deviation exists and no distance-based refund is due however the trip is characterised. The driver is right that the trace figure governs, not the rounded 21.1 km on the trip record, and the trace itself is clean (181 fixes, 10 s cadence, 100% coverage, max_gap_sec 0.0), so POL-RD-07 is not engaged.

2) The SGD 4.00 toll was paid twice and is refunded. The ECP (Fort Rd towards City) gantry is a real crossing — the trace passes it at a nearest-fix distance of 0.0 m at 15:43:10 — so the app line is not a phantom charge, and the SGD 6.00 airport surcharge is properly chargeable because the trip originated at Changi Terminal 3. But the driver also took SGD 4.00 in cash for that same crossing, and his own statement concedes it and asks that the app charge be the one refunded ('If the app also charged, refund him the app one'). POL-RD-09 does not permit a government-set pass-through to be counted twice against the rider, so the SGD 4.00 ERP line on the ledger (EV-FARE-00523) is reversed as a standalone pass-through correction. Charged_total was SGD 38.83; the rider ends up paying the SGD 38.83 the trip properly cost, and the contested SGD 4.00 comes back to him.

3) The driver's request for NO_ACTION is declined for the reason in (2): the duplicate cash collection is a pass-through counted twice, correctable under POL-RD-09 whether or not a deviation exists. There is no repeat-deviation pattern — deviation_flags_90d is 0 over 250 completed trips and the excess is far below the materiality gate — so no POL-RD-06 conduct referral arises; and no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral fires either, because the gantry that was billed was actually crossed. I have not used prior_deviation_flags or any other context-only profile field (POL-GEN-01).

4) The rider's alternative 'off-route ERP' theory is not accepted: no traffic advisory covers this trip (EV-ADVIS-00523-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), so POL-RD-03 cannot exonerate anyone, and no deviation was established in any event. The empty chat log (EV-CHAT-00523, zero messages) means no rider-requested-detour exoneration can be run in either direction, and no extra corroboration is owed to the rider (deviation_claims_60d 0).

Confidence 0.85, above the 0.70 floor. The deciding fact — that the toll was also collected in cash — is carried by the driver's statement, which carries no weight multiplier and so does not lower the confidence cap, together with the full-weight fare ledger. No escalation and no referral is required.

To the Rider and the Driver — this ruling concerns trip TRP-00523 (11 Sep 2026, Changi Airport T3 to Chinatown Point).

Route. The meter charged SGD 38.83 in all (base fare SGD 3.80; distance and time SGD 25.65; Changi airport surcharge SGD 6.00; ERP SGD 4.00; platform fee SGD 0.80). Rider, your sense that the ECP was not the route you would have picked does not change the fare by itself. The GPS trace measures 21.13 km against the platform's 19.8 km optimal route — an excess of 1.33 km, or 6.72%. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to clear both 20% of the optimal distance and 0.8 km. It clears the 0.8 km limb but not the 20% limb, so no route deviation is established and no distance-based refund is due. The trace is unimpaired (181 fixes at 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, no gap over 90 seconds), so POL-RD-07 does not apply and its figures govern. The deviation head of your claim is therefore not supported, which is why this is a partial, not a full, refund.

Toll. The SGD 4.00 you contest is a real ECP (Fort Rd towards City) crossing: the trace carries a fix 0.0 m from that gantry at 15:43:10. This is not a gantry the trace never passed, so POL-RD-09(4)'s phantom-charge limb is not engaged — Driver, your point that the line is metered and matched is accepted. But your own filed statement concedes that you collected the toll in cash and that if the app also charged it, it should be refunded to the rider. The app did charge it (the SGD 4.00 ERP line on the fare breakdown). One toll has been paid twice. POL-RD-09 requires pass-through charges to be settled separately and never counted twice, so the SGD 4.00 app line is returned to the Rider as a pass-through correction; that correction is available whether or not a deviation is established. Your further submission that the fare should simply stand is rejected — it cannot survive your own concession. Rider, note the refund rests on the double payment, not on the ECP lying off the optimal route: a bare off-route ERP claim, with no deviation established and no closure exonerated, refunds nothing under POL-RD-09(2).

Points that did not change the outcome. No repeat-deviation pattern is weighed against the Driver: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 across 250 completed trips in 90 days, so POL-RD-06 is not triggered and no driver-conduct referral arises (lifetime counters such as prior_deviation_flags are context only under POL-GEN-01). The trip's chat log is empty, so no rider-requested detour can be run under POL-RD-04, and the missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00523-01, status MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) leaves no closure exoneration under POL-RD-03. The SGD 6.00 Changi surcharge is properly chargeable because the trip originated at the airport, and because the ERP line is a genuine crossing no billing-integrity referral is produced. Nothing here is escalated: the trace is unimpaired, the trip identifiers match, and no mandatory-escalation trigger fires.

Figures and basis. Charged total SGD 38.83; refunded ERP line SGD 4.00; net returned to the Rider SGD 4.00. The app charge is carried by the fare breakdown (weight 1.0) and corroborated by the GPS trace (weight 1.0); the Driver's statement carries the cash collection and the concession and, having no weight_multiplier, does not enter the confidence cap. Confidence 0.85, above the 0.70 floor.

The trace is sound for POL-RD-07 purposes (181 fixes at a 10 s cadence, 100% coverage, max_gap_sec 0.0), so nothing is impaired and nothing escalates. The driver's routing is not shown to be a closure-forced detour: no traffic advisory covers this trip (EV-ADVIS-00523-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, and its absence is itself citable), so POL-RD-03 has nothing to name and cannot exonerate anything.

(2) The toll was charged twice, and that is refunded. The driver's own filed statement says he told the rider about a cash payment for the ERP ('sometimes the app doesn't capture it') and that if the app also charged it, the app one should be refunded. The fare ledger confirms the app did charge it: the ECP (Fort Rd towards City) line of SGD 4.00 sits on the CHARGED bill with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and the trace shows the vehicle crossing that gantry (nearest fix 0.0 m at 15:43:10). The rider therefore paid SGD 4.00 in cash at the gantry and SGD 4.00 again on the app for one single crossing. POL-RD-09 settles government-set and third-party pass-throughs separately and never twice; the duplicated app line is refunded in full as a standalone pass-through correction, available whether or not a deviation exists. That equals the whole contested SGD 4.00, so the refund is full (charged_total was 38.83; the correction is the 4.00 ERP line).

(3) The driver's counter-arguments are accepted where they go. The gantry is genuinely matched (0.0 m), so the app line is not a phantom gantry under POL-RD-09(4), and the SGD 6.00 Changi airport surcharge is properly chargeable (the trip ORIGINATED at Terminal 3 and ran off-peak on a Friday afternoon). The refund rests not on an unmatched line but on the duplication the driver himself concedes, which is why it is granted even though no deviation is established. No driver compensation is due: billed distance (21.1 km) matches the traced distance, so there is no unbilled shortfall under POL-RD-04.

(4) Profile arguments change nothing. There is no repeat-deviation pattern (driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 across 250 trips in 90 days), so POL-RD-06 is not engaged and its conduct referral does not fire; and the rider's rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, so no extra corroboration burden attaches. ledger.claim: The SGD 4.00 the rider contests is the ERP pass-through line for the ECP (Fort Rd towards City) gantry, and the rider was made to pay that one crossing twice: once in cash at the gantry and again on the app ledger. The driver does not deny the cash collection - his own filed statement says that if the app also charged the toll, 'refund him the app one' - and the payments ledger shows the app did charge it, a SGD 4.00 erp line. POL-RD-09 opens with the rule that government-set and third-party pass-through charges are settled separately and are 'never counted twice'; a duplicate pass-through line is refunded in full as a standalone billing-integrity correction, and POL-RD-09(4) makes that correction available whether or not a deviation exists. No deviation finding is needed to reach it.

The toll the rider is contesting is not a charge their own itinerary would ever have produced. The platform's optimal route for this trip is PIE then Nicoll Hwy and carries zero ERP - optimal_route_erp_sgd is 0.0 - while the gantry actually billed, ECP (Fort Rd towards City) at SGD 4.00, is flagged on_optimal_route false. The rider therefore paid a toll incurred by the driver's routing, not by the rider's journey, and that off-route ERP falls to be corrected as a pass-through under POL-RD-09 rather than left on the rider's bill.

The ECP routing was the driver's election, not a rider instruction. The in-app chat log for this trip carries zero messages and no waypoint_hint, so there is no recorded rider request for the expressway and POL-RD-04's rider-requested-detour exoneration cannot be run at all - on the clause's own terms the corroboration test is undecidable and the clause is unavailable. POL-RD-09(3) withholds an ERP refund only where the detour was rider-caused under POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05 or POL-RD-12; none of those is engaged, so nothing on this record bars correction of the ECP toll.

The driver cannot explain the ECP routing away as a closure-forced detour. No traffic advisory covers this trip at all: EV-ADVIS-00523-01 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0 and fired the issue MISSING_ARTIFACT - I disclose that impairment - and its absence leaves POL-RD-03 with no advisory to name an affected road, no validity window and no shortest-lawful-alternative length to compute a cap from. With no closure, no advisory and no rider instruction, the ECP route and the toll it attracted are simply the driver's own choice, and the absence of the advisory is itself citable.

The gantry crossing itself is real, which is exactly why the app line is the duplicate and not the legitimate charge. The driver's own trace carries a fix 0.0 m from the billed gantry at 15:43:10, so the vehicle passed directly through it and the rider does not dispute that the toll was incurred. What the rider disputes is paying it twice for one crossing - cash at the gantry plus the SGD 4.00 app line - and that single duplicated line is what POL-RD-09 corrects.

I do not overreach on distance, and the rider's case does not need it. The trace excess is 1.33 km, or 6.72%, which is below POL-RD-01's 20% establishment threshold, so no route deviation under POL-RD-01 is established and none is claimed here. The contested SGD 4.00 is the twice-charged ERP line, and that line is corrected under POL-RD-09 on its own footing, independently of any deviation finding.

The rider is not a serial deviation claimant, so no extra corroboration is owed. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, which means the POL-RD-08 uplift that would demand corroboration beyond the gps_trace for a rider with four or more unsubstantiated claims is not engaged. I cite that field only for the POL-RD-08 test that names it, as POL-GEN-01 requires; it is used to show no additional burden attaches, never as a substitute for evidence about this trip.

The deviation fails at the first gate, so the rider's core complaint cannot be sustained. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed BOTH 20% of optimal_distance_km AND 0.8 km absolute, and both tests must pass. On the governing trace figure the excess is 1.33 km — which clears the absolute limb — but it is only 6.72% of the 19.8 km optimal, well under the 20% percentage limb. The percentage test therefore fails, no deviation is established, and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip, save only for a billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4).

The threshold test must be run on the trace figure, not on the rounded convenience copy: POL-RD-01 states that gps_trace.trace_distance_km governs where it and trip_record.actual_distance_km disagree, and that actual_distance_km may NOT be cited for the test. The trace itself is sound — 181 fixes at a 10 s cadence, 100% coverage, max_gap_sec 0.0 and no interruptive gap — so no POL-RD-07 impairment arises and the 21.13 km measurement stands as the basis for the 6.72% excess figure.

The 4.00 ERP line is a genuine metered pass-through, not a billing defect. The ECP (Fort Rd towards City) gantry charged at 15:43:10 is met by the trace at a nearest-fix distance of 0.0 m (fix index 99, timestamp 15:43:10), squarely inside the 250 m match radius POL-RD-09 applies. POL-RD-09(4) permits a billing-integrity refund only for a charge line for a gantry the gps_trace NEVER passes; this trace passes this gantry, so limb (4) is not engaged.

The 6.00 airport surcharge is properly chargeable and is no defect: the trip ORIGINATED at Changi Airport Terminal 3 (pickup label on the trip record), and the fare model makes such a surcharge a billing defect only on a trip that does not originate at an airport. Combined with the trace-matched ERP line, no line of this fare_breakdown is a phantom or unmatched charge, so POL-RD-09(4) has nothing to reach.

The rider's account of an in-app exchange — that the driver recommended the expressway and that he agreed — has no documentary support. The chat log for this trip contains zero messages (message_count 0, first_message_at and last_message_at null), so no rider instruction, no detour request and no discussion of a cash toll appears anywhere in the bundle. POL-RD-08 places the initial burden on the rider and provides that assertions citing no evidence ID carry no weight and are discarded.

Even taking the rider's double-payment account at its highest, the 4.00 app ERP charge is a separate, trace-matched metered pass-through for a gantry the vehicle actually crossed; any cash the driver separately collected is an off-platform cash-handling matter between the parties, not a defective platform fare line. POL-RD-09(4) is the sole refund route POL-RD-01 leaves open where no deviation is established, and it does not authorise refunding a matched gantry — so the rider's own 'paid twice' theory, even if credited, supplies no basis to disturb this fare.

This dispute is rider-filed and the fare_breakdown shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00. POL-GEN-03 makes NO_ACTION party-relative: it leaves the present payment state exactly as it stands and never means 'restore the charge'. The correct outcome on this record therefore leaves the 38.83 charged total, including its 4.00 ERP line, in place in the driver's favour.

No repeat-deviation pattern can be weighed against the driver. POL-GEN-01 forbids substituting the lifetime prior_deviation_flags for that field, so there is no pattern evidence here at all.
